question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${m}^{2}$ and ${n}^{2}$ are perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{m}^{2}{n}^{2}} & =\sqrt{m\cdot m\cdot n\cdot n} \\  & =\sqrt{m\cdot n\cdot m\cdot n} \\  & =\sqrt{(mn)\cdot (mn)} \\  & =\sqrt{(mn)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(mn)^{2}} & =|mn|\end{aligned}
$$
